bug_semantics: An authenticated attacker can persist attacker-controlled HTML or JavaScript in a replication rule comment. The WebUI later treated the returned comment as HTML in two places: the rule-detail page concatenated every rule metadata value into a jQuery-created table-row fragment, and the approval page supplied the raw comments value to DataTables. Viewing the rule or reviewing it for approval therefore executes the stored payload in the WebUI origin.
flaw_origin: The primary's 471794b030d437c3273def7de53b85e7bc84bc35 is the smallest real BIC. That normal single-parent commit created lib/rucio/web/ui/static/rule.js and first wrote the generic unsafe renderer that concatenated data[key] into an HTML fragment before appending it to #t_metadata. The persisted comment source was added later by cebd5b059e8c4629a3ae0b2eccfd922ab906ebd7, and the reviewer's 010746bc16b72313d1e779fa9a15996c44b40a9f later created a second unsafe sink in approve_rules.js. Those commits enabled and copied the same output-encoding flaw, respectively, but neither first wrote the rule-detail sink fixed for this advisory. The BIC is an original new-file change, not an import, move, refactor, revert, or squash aggregate.

For the introducer_sha disagreement, git show 471794b030d437c3273def7de53b85e7bc84bc35 -- lib/rucio/web/ui/static/rule.js lib/rucio/web/ui/templates/rule.html shows both files added and the new success callback appending $('' + key + '' + data[key] + ''). git log --all --reverse -S of that exact fragment starts at 471794b030d437c3273def7de53b85e7bc84bc35; git log --all --follow --reverse for rule.js also starts there. Thus the primary wins over the reviewer, whose 010746bc16b72313d1e779fa9a15996c44b40a9f is the later first writer only of the approval-page copy.

For the introducer_parent disagreement, git cat-file -p 471794b030d437c3273def7de53b85e7bc84bc35 reports the sole parent ed04270cf7a5f71e451f2a196dba47aa8dc15458. git ls-tree -r --name-only of that parent for rule.js and rule.html returns no path, while git diff-tree --name-status for the BIC reports both as A. The reviewer's db48889e085355dbc31657a4719cc49f813c64b7 is instead the direct parent of its rejected later candidate 010746bc16b72313d1e779fa9a15996c44b40a9f.

The later lifecycle checks do not displace the BIC: git show cebd5b059e8c4629a3ae0b2eccfd922ab906ebd7 identifies the later rule-comment storage feature, while git log --all --reverse -S"{'data': 'comments'" for approve_rules.js starts at 010746bc16b72313d1e779fa9a15996c44b40a9f. reasoning: The advisory is one stored-XSS vulnerability with two browser triggers. The causal flaw is rendering server-returned, attacker-controlled data as HTML without output encoding. The primary correctly traced the rule-detail sink all the way to its original new-file first writer; the reviewer stopped at the later approval-page copy and therefore selected the wrong introducer and parent. Direct inspection proves the primary BIC's parent lacks the renderer, and exact history excludes moves, imports, and a decomposable squash. For the fix field, both prior outputs actually converge on b96c1feee372b285c1db881db5bc297a40645b25, and the rerun confirms it is the mainline completion point because it descends from the direct rule-detail fix and adds the approval-table fix. The vulnerable/patched tag pairs reproduce the advisory's three version boundaries. Finally, only the resolved BIC commit object is relevant to AI attribution, and it has no AI signal, so all gates are complete for NOT_AI.
